extra.message: Unsafe pickle.loads on request body — Remote code execution on the application server [verified: pickle.loads runs on attacker-supplied body/GET data gated only by a weak shared-token check; no sanitization limits the object graph, giving RCE.]

Server-side template injection via Jinja2 Template from user input — Remote code execution / full server compromise via Jinja sandbox escape [verified: Jinja2 Template built from string-concatenated `fragment` GET param and rendered, allowing classic SSTI/RCE via template expressions.]

OS command injection via unsanitized host parameter — Arbitrary command execution on the host running the Django app [verified: raw `host` GET param is concatenated into os.system('ping -c 1 '+host) with no escaping, enabling shell metacharacter injection.]

Unrestricted file upload with no type/size validation — Storage of arbitrary/executable content on the server filesystem; potential path issues via unsanitized packet_ref/filename [verified: Uploaded file or packet_ref-named content is saved via FileSystemStorage with no extension/content-type/size validation, permitting arbitrary/executable content storage.]

XXE via lxml parser with entity resolution enabled — Local file disclosure, SSRF, and potential DoS via XML entity expansion [verified: etree.XMLParser explicitly sets load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False on attacker-controlled request.body, a textbook XXE configuration.]

Hardcoded fallback Django SECRET_KEY — Attacker with knowledge of the default key can forge session cookies, password-reset tokens, and CSRF tokens, leading to session hijacking and account takeover [verified: config/settings.py:9 hardcodes a known fallback SECRET_KEY shipped in version control, usable to forge sessions/CSRF/reset tokens if the env var is unset.]

Missing authentication on internal ops data endpoint — Unauthenticated disclosure of internal operational/business data [verified: course_roster_fold_036 has no _wrk_gate call or any auth decorator, yet returns sensitive business/PII-adjacent data to any anonymous requester.]

Open redirect via unvalidated lane parameter — Phishing / credential-harvesting redirects hosted under a trusted domain [verified: `lane` param passed directly to django redirect() with no host/path allowlist, enabling open redirect to attacker-controlled URLs.]

Sensitive Authorization header and body written to logs — Credential/token leakage to anyone with log access (log aggregators, disk access, log-shipping pipelines) [verified: Raw request body and Authorization header are logged at WARNING level in plaintext, exposing credentials to anyone with log access.]

Reflected CORS origin combined with allow-credentials — Any malicious website can make credentialed requests to these endpoints and read responses on behalf of a logged-in victim [verified: Origin header is reflected verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin alongside Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, defeating same-origin protections for credentialed requests.]

TLS certificate verification disabled on outbound request — Man-in-the-middle interception/tampering of server-to-server integration traffic [verified: ssl._create_unverified_context() is used for an outbound HTTPS request, disabling certificate validation and exposing it to MITM.]

DEBUG defaults to True when env var unset — Detailed stack traces and settings values (including secrets referenced in tracebacks) disclosed to unauthenticated users on unhandled errors [verified: config/settings.py:10 defaults DEBUG to True string when DJANGO_DEBUG is unset, with no override elsewhere in the file, exposing detailed error pages by default.]

Missing Secure flag on session/CSRF cookies — Session and CSRF cookies can be intercepted via network eavesdropping or downgrade to HTTP, enabling session hijacking [verified: Lines 85-90 set HttpOnly/SameSite but never set SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE/CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE or SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT, so Django's False defaults apply and cookies can be sent over plain HTTP.]

Non-constant-time comparison of internal auth token — Attacker recovers the shared INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN via timing analysis and gains access to all gated RCE/SSTI/command-injection endpoints [verified: _wrk_gate compares the token with plain `==`, a non-constant-time comparison susceptible to timing side-channel byte-recovery, gating multiple RCE-class endpoints.]

Weak unsalted MD5 hash usage — Trivial reversal/collision of the hashed value if used for any integrity or secrecy purpose [verified: hashlib.md5 with no salt is used to hash a user-supplied phrase, a broken/fast-to-brute-force algorithm for any security-sensitive use.]

Insecure PRNG used to generate security-relevant nonce — Predictable nonce/code values could be brute-forced or guessed, undermining whatever control relies on them [verified: random.choice (non-cryptographic PRNG) generates a security-relevant nonce/code instead of the `secrets` module, making it predictable.]

CSV formula injection in grade export — A student who registers with a name like '=HYPERLINK(...)' or '=cmd|...' gets that payload embedded in the instructor's exported CSV; opening it in Excel can trigger formula execution, data exfiltration, or code execution on the instructor's machine [verified: get_full_name() is written raw into CSV rows with no leading-character sanitization, and registration allows arbitrary first/last name, so a crafted name reaches Excel/Sheets formula execution when opened by staff.]

Unhandled exceptions and non-atomic partial import in enrollment CSV import — A malformed or partially-invalid CSV crashes the request with an unhandled 500 after already committing some Enrollment writes, leaving the import in a partially-applied, non-atomic state and potentially leaking a stack trace if DEBUG is enabled [verified: Loop calls User.objects.get and Cohort.objects.get with no try/except or transaction wrapper, so a bad row raises DoesNotExist as an unhandled 500 after prior rows already committed, confirming non-atomic partial import.]
